acceptance.given: Historical evidence is present while an authorization decision is evaluated.

oracle.expected: The authorization decision accepts authority only from current verified inputs and explicitly classifies historical evidence as non-authorizing.
forbidden: Authorization is granted because of historical evidence.
oracle.observable: The authorization validator's structured decision output identifies current authority inputs and rejects a historical-only authorization basis.

acceptance.then: The decision preserves historical evidence as non-authorizing.
acceptance.when: The toolchain authorization decision validator evaluates a historical-only authority fixture.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the existing authorization negative validator with historical evidence as the sole claimed authority; authorization must be rejected.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The toolchain authorization path must exclude historical evidence from authorization decisions and use only current verified authority.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve decision-record compatibility; rollback restores the previous toolchain implementation without changing stored historical evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: historical evidence available -> current-authority evaluation -> historical source excluded -> authorization decision emitted
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator rejects historical-only authorization and the emitted decision has no historical authorizing source.

acceptance.given: The matrix evaluation is invoked for its six required Matrix Cases.

oracle.expected: The matrix execution set contains an execution for each of six cases and their input identities are pairwise distinct.
forbidden: Two or more Matrix Cases use the same input.
A Matrix Case lacks an input execution.
oracle.observable: The evaluated matrix manifest exposes six case-to-input execution records whose input identities are all distinct.

acceptance.then: All six cases have their own distinct executed input.
acceptance.when: The toolchain matrix evaluator validates the matrix execution manifest.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use a matrix execution manifest with a duplicate input identity or an omitted case execution; the structural matrix validator must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The toolchain matrix evaluator records each required case input and rejects an incomplete or non-pairwise-distinct six-case execution set.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Maintain the evaluation-seed manifest schema and existing consumer compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: matrix evaluation requested -> six case inputs recorded -> completeness and pairwise distinction checked -> aggregate accepted or rejected
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The matrix validator confirms six executions with six pairwise-distinct input identities.

acceptance.given: A supplied target has been substituted for the required target.

oracle.expected: Identity verification rejects the substituted target before target-dependent inspection or replay is dispatched.
forbidden: Treating a substituted target as the required target.
oracle.observable: The target-verification result is rejected or blocked, and the operation trace contains no accepted substituted-target dispatch.

acceptance.then: The substituted-target condition is rejected without a target-dependent operation proceeding.
acceptance.when: The toolchain identity verifier is run against the existing read-only substituted-target selector.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the existing read-only target validator selector with a required/supplied identity mismatch; validation must fail closed before dispatch.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The toolchain replay path compares the supplied target with the required identity and blocks substitution before inspection or replay.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No target identity schema change; rollback restores the preceding toolchain validation implementation.

slice_hint.state_transition: substituted target supplied -> required identity comparison -> mismatch detected -> rejection -> no target operation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The identity validator returns rejected or blocked and records zero accepted operations for the substituted target.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer completed enable, disable, and behavioral rollback.

oracle.expected: That Consumer invokes re-enable through its real call surface and records successful restoration of Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.
forbidden: Re-enable is executed only through a simulated or non-real call surface.
oracle.observable: The Consumer lifecycle trace contains a successful real re-enable call and restoration fields for Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

acceptance.then: The applicable Consumer has re-enabled through its real call surface with the required baseline restored.
acceptance.when: The toolchain Consumer lifecycle integration test executes enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the existing skill replay lifecycle test selector with a trace missing real re-enable or containing simulated-only re-enable; integration validation must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The toolchain consumer lifecycle executes real-call-surface re-enable after rollback and verifies restoration of Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the Consumer lifecycle trace contract and existing route/baseline fields.

slice_hint.state_transition: Consumer rolled back -> real re-enable call -> Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline restored -> successful re-enable recorded
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The integration trace proves the applicable Consumer's real re-enable success and restoration checks.
